title: Working in a curio store and bands advertising downtown
summary: Back in the city he works as porter in a curio store; recalls bands on trucks and balconies advertising for stores.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, when I came to the city I started working on Connell Street as a porter and a curio store and I was very much interested all my life about music and that's how it started. Around the age of about 14 I played drums.
You were working in what kind of store? A curio store.
Curio store where they sold alligators, different little- Oh yeah, curio.
Yeah, curio, that's right. I see. Right next to Waylines. They didn't have any music in there, huh? In the store, never.
No, right next to Waylines, there was music there. Yeah.
Did they have live bands in Waylines then?
No, they had them on the streets, I mean parades and the advertising, bands on the trucks.
Uh-huh. I just wondered, because you hear about music in department stores, you know, did you ever hear any of that when the bands would go in department stores and play?
Somebody told me about it, I guess it was one of the older fellas.
That he used to go in the store and they'd have a band up on the second floor playing for the public.
Well I know different clothes in stores on Ramport and St. Charles so far, and different fellas used to play on the balcony.
